target.title: fix(agents): race in-flight tool promises against run abort (#103905)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103905. When an embedded run aborts, a **non-cooperative** in-flight tool — one whose `execute` never observes the abort signal (e.g. stuck waiting on a subprocess) — keeps the wrapped call pending forever. The run then hangs instead of failing fast, leaving sessions stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

`wrapToolWithAbortSignal` (in `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts`, the wrapper imported by `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` on current main) now races the tool's execute promise against the combined abort signal:

- On abort, the wrapped call **rejects immediately** with an `AbortError` instead of awaiting the tool forever.
- JavaScript cannot cancel a running promise: a non-cooperative tool keeps executing in the background and may settle later, but that late settlement is detached so the result never lands in an aborted run.
- Tool settlements pass through untouched, preserving tool error semantics.

**File note for reviewers:** an earlier review asked to port the race to `src/agents/pi-tools.abort.ts`. Current main has since renamed that file to `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts` (#85341 "internalize OpenClaw agent runtime"), so this PR's rebased diff now lands on the **active** wrapper — verified: `src/agents/agent-tools.ts:28` imports `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` from `./agent-tools.abort.js`.

## User Impact

Aborted runs reject promptly instead of hanging on stuck tool calls; normal tool results are unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof — live abort race (final head `f9f61c2e`, 2026-07-19).

The real `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` was executed via `tsx` (no mocks of the wrapper; a tool stub stands in only for the tool itself):

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx abort-race-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 07:58:49 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
code path: src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts wrapToolWithAbortSignal @ PR head
[non-cooperative] rejected in 101ms after abort: name=AbortError message="Aborted"
[late-settling] aborted call rejected in 101ms: Aborted
[late-settling] background tool later settled=true (detached from aborted run)
[normal] resolved with tool result: {"echoed":{"hello":"world"}}
[result] PASS: abort races in-flight tool promises; normal results unaffected
```

- **Non-cooperative tool** (execute promise never settles): rejects 101ms after the 100ms abort — without the race this call would hang forever.
- **Late-settling tool**: the aborted call rejects promptly; the background tool still settles later (400ms), detached from the aborted run.
- **Normal tool**: result passes through unchanged.

Regression tests (final head):

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-tools.abort.test.ts
```

```text
Tests  14 passed (14)
```

## What was not tested

A full embedded-agent run with a live model provider; the proof exercises the exact wrapper whose await-vs-race behavior this PR changes.

## Rebase status

Rebased onto latest `origin/main` at head `f9f61c2e`; the rename of `pi-tools.abort.ts` → `agent-tools.abort.ts` means the rebased diff targets the active wrapper on current main.

target.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention
target.body:
Closes #105625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Gateways retaining many completed background bash/exec sessions would keep an unbounded finished-session map until TTL expiry, and session reset/delete would leave matching finished process records pollable until that TTL. That multiplies retained aggregate output and can grow gateway heap under bursty shell workloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep completed `process poll` / `process log` aggregates (ClawSweeper rejected tail-only retention), but enforce deterministic finished-session count and total-aggregate-byte caps, and purge finished records whose `scopeKey` matches gateway session lifecycle cleanup keys. Shared scopes (for example chat bash) are not purged when an unrelated agent session resets.

## User Impact

Operators get bounded finished-process memory growth under heavy background exec traffic. Resetting or deleting a gateway session no longer leaves that session’s finished process records pollable until job TTL. Completed process log/poll behavior for still-retained sessions is unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS Darwin arm64 (live runtime harness on PR head + focused unit tests)

Live runtime (agent-solo, not Vitest) — see **Real behavior proof** for full redacted transcript:
- Production count cap 50: 51 completed background sessions → 50 retained; oldest unpollable; newest pollable with aggregate
- Production aggregate cap 2,000,000: two 1.2M sessions → only newest retained (1.2M total)
- Scoped reset: `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` → `finishedProcessSessionsCleared=1`; `chat:bash` retained

Focused tests (pass, supplemental):
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` — 8 passed

Static:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

Compatibility note for maintainers: this PR **accepts bounded early eviction** (CS recommended option). Completed process poll/log may disappear before TTL when budgets are exceeded; refine thresholds only if a longer delayed-poll contract is required.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Finished bash process sessions are hard-capped (50 sessions / 2,000,000 aggregate characters) so completed `process poll`/`process log` retention cannot grow unbounded until TTL; session reset/delete purges finished records only for matching lifecycle `scopeKey` values (shared scopes such as `chat:bash` stay).
- Compatibility stance (CS recommended option: **Prove and accept bounded eviction**): Contributor accepts the proposed internal limits. Under burst load, completed process poll/log records may become unavailable **before** the existing job TTL once the 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded. Thresholds are intentionally product-owned if maintainers later want a longer delayed-poll window.
- Environment: local macOS Darwin arm64, Node v24.17.0, PR head `683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256` on branch `fix/105625-bash-finished-session-bounds`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `pruneFinishedSessions` only deletes by TTL; `finishedSessions` has no count/byte cap; `clearSessionResetRuntimeState` does not touch finished process records, so scoped finished sessions remain pollable until TTL.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch (live runtime harness, **not** Vitest):
  1. Load production owner modules from this checkout: `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts` via `tsx`.
  2. Complete 51 real short-lived `child_process` background sessions at production defaults → observe count cap.
  3. Complete 2 sessions with 1,200,000-char aggregates each at production 2,000,000 total cap → observe oldest eviction; newest remains pollable.
  4. Complete three scoped finished sessions (`agent:main:main`, `chat:bash`, `agent:other:main`) and call `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` (same helper gateway session reset/delete uses).
- Evidence after fix (redacted live transcript, 2026-07-13T05:21:16Z UTC):

```text
=== Live runtime proof: finished bash session retention bounds ===
host: darwin arm64
node: v24.17.0
branch_head: 683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256
method: real child_process echo sessions; production finished caps 50 / 2_000_000; not Vitest
redaction: no tokens/paths/IPs; synthetic ids only

--- A) count cap at production default (50 sessions) ---
completed_background_execs: 51
finished_retained_count: 50
count-00_pollable: false
count-50_pollable: true
count-50_aggregate: "out-50\n"
count_cap_ok: true

--- B) aggregate-char cap at production default (2_000_000) ---
sessions_completed: 2 x 1200000 chars
finished_retained_count: 1
retained_ids: bytes-new
total_aggregated_chars: 1200000
bytes-old_pollable: false
bytes-new_pollable: true
aggregate_cap_ok: true

--- C) clearSessionResetRuntimeState scoped finished-process purge ---
before_reset finished_count=3
before match=true shared=true other=true
reset_keys: ["agent:main:main"]
finishedProcessSessionsCleared: 1
after_reset finished_count=2
after match=false shared=true other=true
scoped_reset_ok: true

=== summary ===
count_cap_ok=true
aggregate_cap_ok=true
scoped_reset_ok=true
overall_ok=true
```

- Control check: Scope purge only matches exact `scopeKey` values; `chat:bash` and `agent:other:main` remain after resetting `agent:main:main`. Retained finished sessions keep full `aggregated` (not tail-only) for poll/log.
- Observed result after fix: Oldest finished sessions are evicted under production count and total-aggregate caps while retained entries stay pollable; session-reset runtime cleanup removes only matching-scope finished process records and reports `finishedProcessSessionsCleared`.
- Supplemental focused unit tests (still pass; not a substitute for the live harness above):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- What was not tested: Full multi-tenant Control UI reset UX; sustained multi-hour production heap profile under mixed channel traffic (live harness exercises the same in-process registry and reset cleanup path the Gateway process uses).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation and proof follow ClawSweeper guidance on #105625 (count-plus-byte retention + scope-keyed cleanup; keep completed aggregates).
